video_goal: Personalize a ceramic mug by prepping the surface, drawing with oil-based paint markers, and curing the design in an oven.
required_subjects_and_props: Plain white ceramic mug, oil-based paint markers, rubbing alcohol, cotton pads, cotton swabs, scrap paper, kitchen oven.

outline_steps.visual_action: Hand wipes the exterior surface of a plain white ceramic mug using a cotton pad soaked in rubbing alcohol.
Hand rubs a dry microfiber cloth over the wet areas of the mug until the surface is completely matte and dry.
Hand vigorously shakes a capped oil-based paint marker up and down.
Hand presses the tip of the oil-based marker repeatedly onto a piece of scrap paper until colored paint flows down into the white nib.
The marker tip draws a thick, opaque line directly onto the curved exterior of the ceramic mug.
Hand switches to a fine-tip oil-based marker and draws small dots and accent lines around the initial design.
A cotton swab dipped in rubbing alcohol carefully wipes away a small, wet paint smudge on the mug's surface.
Hand places the fully painted mug onto a wooden table and pulls away, leaving it to air dry.
Hand places the painted ceramic mug directly onto the center metal rack inside a cold, unheated kitchen oven.
Hand turns the oven temperature dial to the 350 degrees setting.
Hand presses the digital buttons on the oven interface to set a bake timer for 30 minutes.
Hand turns the oven dial to the 'Off' position, leaving the oven door slightly ajar with the mug still resting on the rack inside.
Hand lifts the fully cooled, personalized ceramic mug out of the oven and rotates it under a light to show the glossy, cured paint design.
